@@ -106,3 +106,20 @@ else

+# Metrics regeneration is another post-close workspace by-product. It is always
+# attempted after the durable close, and failures are loud but non-fatal: a
+# successful close must never be reported as failed because an artifact or push
+# needs manual recovery.
+if [ "$SCORE" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "hive-close: --no-score — metrics regeneration still runs."
+fi
+if "$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-metrics" "$PROJECT" </dev/null; then
+  echo "hive-close: metrics regenerated"
+else
+  {
+    echo
+    echo "hive-close: WARNING the close SUCCEEDED and is durable on the spine — metrics regeneration did not."
+    echo "  Recover with: hive-metrics $PROJECT"
+  } >&2
+fi

 # Scoped by pathspec to the project's metrics dir, so unrelated work in the
 # operator's clone is never swept into the commit. Nothing staged is a SUCCESS,
 # not an error: hive-metrics is deterministic, so re-running it on an unchanged
-# spine prefix legitimately produces no diff. Push mirrors hive-answer's
-# retry (push -> pull --rebase -> push) and reports precisely how far it got, so
+# spine prefix legitimately produces no diff. A push failure is deliberately a
+# refusal: metrics are a shared path and this helper must never rebase unattended.
+# It reports precisely how far it got, so
 # "committed locally" is never mistaken for "on the hub".
 commit_metrics() {  # commit_metrics <project> <commit-message>  -> 0 committed/nothing-to-do, non-zero otherwise
   local msg="$2" spec="projects/$1/metrics"
@@ -230,16 +231,42 @@ commit_metrics() {  # commit_metrics <project> <commit-message>  -> 0 committed/
   git -C "$OPS_WS" commit --quiet -m "$msg" -- "$spec" \
     || { echo "hive: git commit failed for $spec in $OPS_WS (git identity unset, a commit hook, or an index lock?)" >&2; return 1; }
   if ! git -C "$OPS_WS" push --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
-    if ! git -C "$OPS_WS" pull --rebase --quiet; then
-      echo "hive: push failed and rebase failed — committed locally in $OPS_WS, NOT on the hub; resolve by hand" >&2
-      return 1
-    fi
-    git -C "$OPS_WS" push --quiet \
-      || { echo "hive: push failed for $OPS_WS — committed locally, NOT on the hub" >&2; return 1; }
+    echo "hive: push failed — committed locally in $OPS_WS, NOT on the hub; resolve the shared metrics branch manually (fetch, reconcile, then push)" >&2
+    return 1
   fi
   echo "  committed + pushed: $spec ($msg)"
 }
 
+# Parse the Predictions section used by both hive-launch and hive-score. Keep the
+# regexes in one place: a gate and its calibration reader that disagree recreate
+# retro 2 D1. Results are placed in globals because callers need both the parsed
+# fields and the section text for diagnostics.
+# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # outputs are consumed by sourced callers
+parse_predictions() {  # parse_predictions <order-file>
+  local file="$1" block
+  PREDICTIONS_SECTION=0 PREDICTIONS_BLOCK=""
+  PRED_EFFORT_TXT="" PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT="" PRED_REVIEW_TXT=""
+  [ -f "$file" ] || die "order file not found: $file"
+  if grep -qE '^##[[:space:]]*Predictions[[:space:]]*$' "$file"; then
+    PREDICTIONS_SECTION=1
+    block=$(awk '
+      /^##[ \t]*Predictions[ \t]*$/ { inblock = 1; next }
+      inblock && /^#/                { inblock = 0 }
+      inblock                        { print }
+    ' "$file")
+    PREDICTIONS_BLOCK="$block"
+    PRED_EFFORT_TXT=$( { printf '%s' "$block" | grep -oiE 'Expected effort:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9.–—-]*[[:space:]]*worker-hours?' | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected effort:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+    PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT=$( { printf '%s' "$block" | grep -oiE 'Expected questions:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9–—-]*' | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected questions:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+    PRED_REVIEW_TXT=$( { printf '%s' "$block" | grep -oiE 'Expected review outcome:[[:space:]]*[^.]+' | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected review outcome:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+  fi
+  PREDICTIONS_FIELDS=0
+  for t in "$PRED_EFFORT_TXT" "$PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT" "$PRED_REVIEW_TXT"; do
+    if [ -n "$t" ]; then
+      PREDICTIONS_FIELDS=$((PREDICTIONS_FIELDS + 1))
+    fi
+  done
+}

 # The folded board as a JSON array (board-view --json): the machine projection —
 # one object per task with task/status/owner/depends_on/review. This is the read
 # path the tooling parses instead of the rendered table: a task id wider than the
diff --git a/scripts/hive-launch b/scripts/hive-launch
index 6de9fd9..b6873b4 100755
--- a/scripts/hive-launch
+++ b/scripts/hive-launch
@@ -58,6 +58,31 @@ load_project_conf "$PROJECT"
 TASK=$(task_from_order "$REL")

+# The predictions gate is deliberately before every board write. It calls the
+# same parser as hive-score; an absent section remains a recorded metric, while
+# a present section with no parseable scored field is an authoring failure unless
+# the operator explicitly uses --anyway or declares the task unpredicted.
+parse_predictions "$OPS_WS/$REL"
+if [ "$PREDICTIONS_SECTION" -eq 1 ] && [ "$PREDICTIONS_FIELDS" -eq 0 ]; then
+  if ! grep -qiE 'deliberately[[:space:]-]+unpredicted' <<<"$PREDICTIONS_BLOCK"; then
+    {
+      echo "hive-launch: refusing '$REL' — ## Predictions is present but none of the three scored fields parse."
+      echo "  Use the four literal protocol labels:"
+      echo "    - Expected effort:"
+      echo "    - Expected questions:"
+      echo "    - Expected review outcome:"
+      echo "    - Named risks: (required, but intentionally unscored)"
+      echo "  Offending Predictions lines:"
+      printf '%s\n' "$PREDICTIONS_BLOCK" | sed 's/^/    /'
+      echo "  Fix the order, declare it deliberately unpredicted, or override with --anyway."
+    } >&2
+    [ -n "$ANYWAY" ] || exit 1
+    echo "hive-launch: WARNING --anyway overriding an unparseable Predictions section" >&2
+  fi
+elif [ "$PREDICTIONS_SECTION" -eq 1 ] && [ "$PREDICTIONS_FIELDS" -lt 3 ]; then
+  echo "hive-launch: WARNING Predictions section is partial ($PREDICTIONS_FIELDS of 3 scored fields parsed); missing fields remain a calibration gap." >&2
+fi
+
 # Both ids flow into a generated shell wrapper (baked identity), tmux window
 # names, and filesystem paths. Constrain them to a safe charset so a stray
 # metacharacter can neither break nor hijack the worker's write path.

@@ -521,6 +542,19 @@ check "beta effort prediction quoted" "entry beta | grep -q '4 worker-hours'"

 check "beta absent field unpredicted" "[ \"\$(verdict beta questions)\" = unpredicted ]"
 
+# The launch gate and scorer source the same parser. Exercise the parser directly
+# on the malformed dialect and compare its zero-field verdict with the scorer's
+# section-present coverage vocabulary; Named risks is visible but remains outside

+# shellcheck source=scripts/hive-common.sh
+source "$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-common.sh"
+parse_predictions "$ORDERS/2026-07-20-malformed.md"

+check "shared parser keeps Named risks unscored" "grep -qF 'Named risks' '$ORDERS/2026-07-20-malformed.md' && grep -qF 'PREDICTIONS_FIELDS' '$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-common.sh'"
+check "launch and score call the shared parser" "grep -qF 'parse_predictions' '$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-launch' && grep -qF 'parse_predictions' '$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-score'"

+expect_fail_msg "bogus review verdict refused" "clean | minor rework | rework" "$S" alpha --again --review bogus

sources.exit: runner wall clock at process reap
sources.first_response: timestamp of the first byte the agent wrote to stdout or stderr
